purpose: Independent verification of external review REVIEW-1.md; 7 read-only agents, every claim recomputed from repo artifacts

claims.claim: (a) The preregistered primary endpoint was semantic equivalence to the gold statement, but the implemented equivalence grader is a stub that never runs.
claims.evidence: Preregistration docs/research/BRIDGE-EXPERIMENT.md: Tier 1 header (line 64) is 'PRIMARY', grading rule 1 (lines 79-80) is 'faithful@budget = typechecks AND BEq+-equivalent to gold (ProofNetVerif...)', and lines 90-91 preregister 'Success = D>E on faithful@budget (p<.05) AND D≤E on tokens-to-solve' — the primary endpoint is semantic equivalence ∧ typecheck. In the scorer, bench/score_bridge.py:198-201 the equivalence leg is literally: `def judge_stub(task, run): """TODO(judge): BEq+ / LLM equivalence of output_lean vs task['gold_formal']...""" return None` — it always returns None and per lines 222-225 a None leg is skipped in the success fold, so equivalence never enters any score. I verified it never ran: `find bench/data -name '*.judge.json'` returns 0 files across all 2,355 run rows; docs/research/BRIDGE-RESULTS.md:5 says 'judge/BEq+ leg is PENDING human calibration and no judge number appears here'; BRIDGE-REPORT.md:463-464 concedes 'The preregistered faithful@budget metric (BEq+ equivalence) was never graded'. One nuance: a separate LLM-judge harness exists as real code (bench/judge_bridge.py, dual strict/evaluated grading, writes <task>.judge.json) — more than a stub — but it produced zero verdicts in the repo, and its own docstring says the BEq+ primary 'rig' never landed. The substance of the claim holds exactly.

claims.claim: (b) Actual success = produced declaration AND no hallucinated (nonexistent) cited names AND typechecks (bench/score_bridge.py ~190-230).
claims.evidence: bench/score_bridge.py:219-225 (inside score_run): `proxy = bool(lean) and not errored and len(hallucinated) == 0; success = proxy; for leg in (tc, jd): if leg is not None: success = success and leg`. Since jd (judge) is always None and tc (typecheck via the pinned-toolchain REPL rig) returned real booleans in the campaign, implemented success = produced ∧ no-runner-error ∧ zero hallucinated citations ∧ typecheck-ok. The stored bench/data/bridge_summary.json confirms: success_metric = 'produced ∧ no-halluc ∧ TYPECHECK (judge pending calibration)' with typecheck_ok_k 270/260/340/325/332 for arms A-E. I reproduced the report's headline tables from its paired_matrix: Tier-1a (371 non-fresh tasks) success A 59.6% B 57.1% C 62.3% D 64.2% E 60.9% (report prints D as 64.1 — rounding of 238/371=64.15%); Tier-1b (100 fresh) 20/22/25/42/16%; McNemar D-vs-E discordants 32-vs-6 fresh and 63-vs-51 eval — all matching BRIDGE-REPORT.md §4.1-4.2. Two immaterial details beyond the claim's wording: success also requires the run row to have no error flag, and names in the verified-renames list ('renamed', historically real) are not counted as hallucinated (classify(), lines 105-113).

claims.claim: (c) The report's claim that 'typechecking alone never counts as success' is technically true but misleading, since nothing checks semantic faithfulness.
claims.evidence: Both factual components are confirmed: the report's abstract (BRIDGE-REPORT.md:21-22, 'Grading is mechanical throughout, and typechecking alone never counts as success') and §3 (line 100, 'Typecheck is never success by itself') are technically true — success additionally requires a produced declaration and zero hallucinated citations (score_bridge.py:219-225) — and no semantic-faithfulness check runs anywhere in Tier-1 success (judge always None, BEq+ never built, 0 judge verdict files). The 'misleading' characterization is where I part ways with the reviewer: the full report explicitly discloses the gap. §3 lines 104-107 say the preregistered LLM-judge faithfulness leg was 'quarantined... behind a human-calibration gate and ultimately dropped', and §8 limitation 5 (lines 463-471) states outright that faithful@budget 'was never graded' and that Tier-1 'success' 'can still reward a well-formed wrong statement; the Tier-1 fresh-set numbers are best read jointly with the hallucination and trace evidence.' The kernel of truth: the abstract itself carries no such caveat, so a reader of the abstract alone would not learn that the semantic-equivalence leg is absent — 'typechecking alone never counts as success' there could be read as implying a faithfulness check exists. Misleading-in-the-abstract, disclosed-in-the-body.

claims.claim: Tier-1 arm D has the decl_exists existence verifier and arm E has no equivalent tool.
claims.evidence: bench/arms/mcp-D.json gives arm D the full remote wikibrain MCP (https://wikilean.jackmccarthy.org/mcp); its tool list (wiki/src/mcp.ts line 249) includes decl_exists ('Verify Lean decl names against the doc-gen4 declaration index BEFORE citing them'), and bench/run_benchmark.py lines 60-66 explicitly allowlist mcp__wikibrain__decl_exists for D (used via ARM_TOOLS['D'] in bench/run_bridge.py line 74). Arm E (bench/arms/mcp-E.json) gets only wiki_mcp.py (wiki_search, wiki_get, nlab_search — TOOLS dict at line 208) plus formal_mcp.py (loogle, decl_grep, decl_read — TOOLS dict at line 263); none is an existence verifier. Nuance: E's loogle accepts a bare name and decl_grep can grep declaration headers, so existence can in principle be checked indirectly by search, but there is no dedicated batch verifier keyed to the scoring oracle, and E's fresh transcripts show no decl_exists-style usage (0 calls). All built-in tools (Bash/Read/Grep/WebSearch/etc.) are disallowed for every arm (run_benchmark.py DISALLOWED_TOOLS).

claims.claim: Hallucination-free citations are themselves a component of the success metric (score_bridge.py), so D holds a tool that optimizes part of its own score.
claims.evidence: bench/score_bridge.py line 221: proxy = bool(lean) and not errored and len(hallucinated) == 0; lines 222-225 make success = proxy AND typecheck AND judge (when those legs return non-None). So zero hallucinated citations is a hard conjunct of both success_proxy and success. The scorer's Oracle (lines 47-49, 70-113) classifies cited names against the doc-gen4 declaration-data.json index plus catalog/data/decl_renames.jsonl — the same doc-gen4 decl index and rename map that the decl_exists tool queries (wiki/src/brain-api.ts lines 1431 'the doc-gen4 oracle GET /decl uses' and 1454 referencing catalog/data/decl_renames.jsonl). Arm D therefore has in-run query access to (effectively) the same oracle the scorer applies post-hoc for the no-hallucination component.

Headline framing — Abstract lines 29-32: "a Sonnet agent given the union of bridge and formal-search tools, plus a manual distilled from measured tool behavior, sets the best rows we know of on both benchmarks (R@10 0.885; group-recall@10 0.557 against the specialist SOTA of 0.461)"; §5.1 line 268: "WF is decisive. claims.claim: The paired significance tests on MathlibQR treat all 810 query rows as independent observations (pairing/resampling unit = the query row, not the underlying declaration).
claims.evidence: score_retrieval.py computes no significance test; the QR paired numbers live in the reports (docs/research/bridge-report/report.tex lines 403-416, BRIDGE-REPORT.md line 261, BRIDGE-RESULTS.md line 65: 'F and W are statistically tied (paired discordants 78 F-only vs. 66 W-only, exact p = 0.36)'; WF beats F 71 vs 27, p=1.0e-5, and W 83 vs 27, p=8.3e-8; limitations item: 'F-vs-W on QR is a null at n=810 (p=0.36)'). I reproduced all three exactly by pairing per qid (declID__style) over run rows in bench/v2/runs/agent/qr810/{F,W,WF} with hit = gold ∈ top-10, then the exact binomial (sign) test used in recompute_figdata.py's mcnemar(): n_paired=810; F vs W 78/66, p=0.359; WF vs F 71/27, p=1.01e-5; WF vs W 83/27, p=8.31e-8. The pairing unit is therefore the individual query row, all 810 treated as independent Bernoulli pairs — yet the 144 F/W discordant rows come from only 76 distinct declarations, with 41 declarations contributing >1 discordant row, and neither report nor scripts mention or adjust for this declaration-level clustering (grep for independen/cluster/iid in report.tex and BRIDGE-REPORT.md finds nothing relevant). Note: the Tier-1 McNemar in bench/score_bridge.py (mcnemar(), lines 318-337) pairs by statement-task id and is a separate, unaffected computation — the independence issue is specific to the QR-810 row-level tests.
